claims.statement: dcode is installed by the bundled curl installer and launched with `dcode`; DEEPAGENTS_CODE_EXTRAS selects optional model providers at installation.
dcode trusts launch-directory project artifacts before approval prompts, so untrusted repositories require a remote sandbox for execution isolation.
Default launch is the interactive Textual TUI; `-m`, `-s`, and `--startup-cmd` respectively supply a prompt, skill, and pre-prompt shell command.
`-n` runs one headless task; shell is disabled unless --shell-allow-list is set, and quiet/no-stream are headless-only output controls.
`--acp` runs an ACP server over stdio instead of the Textual UI.
Headless-only turn, timeout, and rubric controls require -n or piped input; turn-budget and timeout expiry use exit 124.
Interactive approval modes are manual, auto, and yolo; invalid persisted values fail closed to manual.
Shift+Tab cycles Manual, Auto, YOLO and omits Auto when ineligible and YOLO when disabled.
Auto and yolo flags are mutually exclusive, require acknowledgement for yolo, and are warned as ineffective in headless mode.
The Auto classifier resolves from CLI, environment, config, then main model; weaker classifiers weaken review.
YOLO requires an acknowledgement per policy version and has a persistent indicator even when its toast is suppressed.
get_checkpointer provides AsyncSqliteSaver over a module-owned connection and drains it after interrupted connection.
Session state is in cached global SQLite path DEFAULT_STATE_DIR/sessions.db.
New thread IDs are naturally sortable UUID7 strings.
Thread listing reads compact metadata through a covering index to avoid blob I/O; index creation failure leaves a slower correct query.
Bare `-r` means the most recent thread; `-r <ID>` targets that thread.
TUI resume resolves recent or explicit threads, prompts for differing cwd, suggests matching unknown IDs, and falls back to a new thread on misses or DB errors.
Private checkpoint channels rehydrate tokens, effective model state, and goal/rubric lifecycle without replaying history.
Model-turn channels are written with the model-response checkpoint, so a resumed checkpoint has point-in-time rather than thread-aggregate values.
Headless runs have no resume/thread-ID input and generate a fresh thread.
`threads list` and `threads delete` manage persisted threads without launching an agent.
COMMANDS.md catalogs 45 public and two hidden debug slash commands.
Hooks are trusted user-privilege shell commands receiving JSON lifecycle payloads and controlling behavior through stdout and exit code.
Matching hooks run concurrently across project, user, and plugin scopes but results reduce in that order; plugins still execute after earlier stops.
Hook events are client or server owned and include tool, compaction, stop, and subagent lifecycle events.
New plugin server hooks take effect after `/reload` because server event registration is fixed at session start.
Hook exit 2 is event-specific blocking, other failures are diagnostics, and JSON output can provide decisions, context, and continuation control.
Project hooks need workspace trust; interactive sessions prompt and may persist trust, while headless/CI must use --trust-project-hooks.
MCP explicit configuration is highest precedence, --no-mcp disables loading, and project stdio/remote servers require trust or approval.
Sandbox selection defaults to local none; bare --sandbox resolves config default and IDs, snapshots, and setup target environments.
Unusable or unenforceable managed policy blocks normal operations with exit 78, while config, doctor, auth path, and help are diagnostic exceptions.
Threads dispatch precedes session launch and warns but queries an explicitly nonexistent cwd filter.
Headless mode uses an autonomous prompt, supports startup skill/command, and returns 1 for unavailable, unreadable, or empty skills.
Focused tests cover headless turn limits, threads cwd behavior, and covering-index use for thread listing.

Interactive and headless clients use server_session to serialize ServerConfig, scaffold a temporary checkpointer workspace, start and await a local LangGraph server, return RemoteAgent, and clean failed startup.
Headless permission hooks disable automatic approval and shell-only interruption shortcuts so gated calls reach hook handlers.
